scope: Independent read-only offline statistics review on source host 380G10. No guest access, workload, build, test, repository script, or archived summarize.py was executed. Original archived records were projected with tar/jq; arithmetic and CSV parsing were performed independently in tool orchestration.

original_record_checks.TclEpochDeltas: Each measured TCLock delegated count equals after.delegated-before.delegated; parks are after.parks-before.parks.
original_record_checks.hash_oracle: For each RCUHT record, hash_integrity_ok is true; all before/after differences are nonnegative; completed equals delta total equals moves+conflicts+misses; total equals the first three outcome counters at each endpoint; all 12 unused counters are zero.

identity.provider_binary_boundary: Separate cacheline and RCUHT provider ELF hashes are retained. Identical source manifests do not establish byte-identical binaries; no workload metrics are pooled.
identity.null_fields_explanation: spin_contention_pct is not recorded for mutex; Native/TCLock lack KD-only entry-ratio and prefetch settings; native has no delegation batch limit. These are explicit nonapplicable backend fields, not silently missing shared identities.

host_review.frequency_policy: intel_cpufreq / ondemand, 800000..3600000 kHz; fixed-frequency operation was not established.

host_review.topology: 64 vCPUs, host CPUs 0..63 exactly pinned, 2 sockets/NUMA nodes of 32 cores. Worker sets are CPU prefixes 0..N-1: 1/8/32 workers stay on node 0; 60 workers span 32 node-0 and 28 node-1 CPUs. Collector and QEMU service threads use CPU 63.

scientific_limits: There is no paired run of the previous 256-byte KD mutex under the same source, topology, workloads, call shell, and instrumentation. This screen compares the compact implementation with Native and TCLock; it cannot isolate performance change caused by shrinking the inline object or adding auxiliary state.
Each backend/workload/thread group has only three 2-second sessions. The displayed spread is a descriptive range, not a confidence interval. Short-run variation is substantial in several groups.

Use whole-run medians as the primary measure. At c01/32, KD whole median is 3.145104 Mops and peak median is 7.276117 Mops; individual selected-peak/whole ratios reach 2.313474. At c08/60, KD peak spread is 60.009446% and whole spread is 39.715100%. Selected 300-ms windows after a 300-ms settling exclusion do not establish sustained throughput.

Every worker progresses in every whole run and selected peak, but that does not prove fairness or absence of starvation over longer runs. Native c08/32 repeat 0 has whole-run worker counts from 117248 to 2791936, about a 23.81 max/min ratio; the largest worker completes 29.6972% of all operations.

Worker geometry changes at 60 workers from one NUMA node to two. Scaling effects cannot be attributed solely to thread count. Actual QEMU page placement is imperfect despite bind policy, and changes slightly between the retained pre/post receipts.

Host ondemand frequency policy was unchanged, but frequency was not fixed and per-session effective clock histories were not measured. Two first-repeat native single-worker sessions have about 44.6-44.8% whole-run spread; the evidence does not identify a causal explanation.

Native and TCLock use C call shells while KD uses its clobber cookie shell. The private benchmark provider includes observation counters and progress sampling; zero diagnostic/PMU/perf flags do not make these uninstrumented production timing results.

RCUHT outcome sums and integrity are exact and outcome proportions are near 25% move / 25% conflict / 50% miss. This validates the recorded payload oracle, not general application behavior or latency distributions.

Weighted KD returned-JIT and TCLock delegation shares are measured across the whole eligible interval, not in the selected peak windows. TCLock parks count successful parking CAS transitions, not context switches or sleep duration.

All 328 source manifest entries agree across the two workload collections, but the retained KD provider ELF hashes differ. Keep each workload and its binary identity separate; do not pool throughput across workloads.
